[ 01 / PROJECT OVERVIEW ]MADE FOR PEOPLE.

Project overview.

Roomies brings shared expenses, chores, groceries and household plans into one mobile space. Designed for housemates in India, the concept includes a local interactive prototype with 36 screens.

THE PEOPLE

Housemates coordinating shared spending, changing schedules and the everyday work of keeping a home running.

THE SCOPE

UX strategy, mobile interface design, shared-home journeys, visual identity and a local interactive prototype.

THE STATUS

Design concept.
UX/UI and interaction design.

[ 02 / THE PROBLEM ]MADE FOR PEOPLE.

The problem.

Shared living creates coordination work that can disappear between group chats, private lists and informal reminders. Housemates need to understand what they owe, who owns a task, which groceries are being picked up and what has changed. Different schedules and split preferences make that shared context especially important.

[ 03 / THE SOLUTION ]MADE FOR PEOPLE.

The solution.

Bring expenses, chores, groceries and household plans into one mobile space. Pair each shared action with a responsible person and a visible state. Allow bill details and shares to be reviewed before saving, make chore ownership explicit, connect grocery claims with shopping lists and keep changes in a shared activity history. Payments remain external to the prototype.

[ 04 / DESIGN PRIORITIES ]MADE FOR PEOPLE.

A few priorities.
A clearer direction.

Three priorities that guide the experience.

01

Make shared costs visible.

Keep bill details and flexible shares understandable before saving.

02

Show who owns it.

Make task ownership and changes visible to the whole household.

03

Keep everyone in the loop.

Connect grocery claims, shared plans and activity history.

[ 08 / REFLECTION & VALIDATION ]MADE FOR PEOPLE.

Designed with intent.
Open to learning.

The study includes four hypotheses and two illustrative proto-personas, not interviewed participants. Interviews, a household diary and task-based usability sessions are proposed to test fairness, ownership, grocery duplication and shared context.

  • Record an expense with shares that add up.
  • Assign or reassign a household chore.
  • Claim groceries before a shopping run.
  • Record an external payment and understand the balance.

A local design prototype. Payments happen outside Roomies. The settlement screen is an empty state; no measured reduction in reminders or household conflict is claimed.
